items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name (Heather) even once, despite a 6+ minute call
No agenda-setting statement or explicit 'sound good?' confirmation to frame the call
No discovery at all on the actual move — never asked home size, stairs/floors, additional rooms, packing needs, boxes, storage, additional stops, access concerns, or moving stressors
Gave only a rough flat ballpark total ($2,000-$2,500) instead of the 'pricing is super simple' hourly-rate breakdown

Never explained what's included (gas, truck, insurance, wrap pads, tools) or the No Worries Damage Coverage — a major miss since the customer volunteered a prior damage claim that Einstein compensated her for
No mention of Meet Your Mover or On-Time Guarantee differentiators
No clock explanation (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute prorated increments, sense-check)
No typical time range, mover/truck count, or variables walkthrough for the estimate
No prep/Save Your Ass speech (consolidation tips, take-a-carload tip) to lower the customer's cost
No attempt to schedule/lock in the move, no 'no deposit required' mention, no email handoff, and no 'any other questions' or hours/contact close
top_strength: Garrison was refreshingly honest when the customer pushed on cost, telling her straight that U-Haul/DIY would genuinely be cheaper for her dad's situation — that candor visibly built trust ('since you're being so honest with me') and kept the call warm even as it moved toward a non-booking outcome.
coaching_note: When the customer volunteered a past damage claim Einstein compensated her for, that was a built-in opening to explain the No Worries Damage Coverage and other differentiators before ceding the sale to U-Haul — Garrison should still run pricing/differentiators and attempt to book even when a customer sounds like they're leaning DIY.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm, affirming language ('Absolutely', 'I see', 'Oh, no') and honest, empathetic answers kept the customer comfortable and appreciative through to a friendly close.
